title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We revise and clarify a preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated device CLI under adversarially mutated intents. The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in per-intent validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). The frozen run used a single generator (gpt-5-mini), a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes=300; completed episodes=282; complete paired outcomes analyzed=141). Observed outcomes: baseline accepted 135/141 = 0.95745; guarded accepted 141/141 = 1.0; paired difference = 0.04255319; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.01418440, 0.07801418]. We incorporate reviewer-requested reconciliations: (1) explicit statement reconciling the preregistration's natural-language directional hypothesis with the registered formal estimand and the observed sign of the effect, (2) an explicit per-condition pipeline timeline with artifact references demonstrating shared_initial_candidate reuse and provider-call accounting, and (3) an explicit declaration of the protocol deviation that the archived model configuration left sampling temperature unset and the practical consequences for deterministic reproduction. Major limitations (synthetic tasks, single model and validator, and an unexecuted benign-control) constrain external generalization. All numeric claims below are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts cited in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs promise to translate operator intent into network device CLI, potentially reducing NetOps workload but introducing syntax, topology and semantic risks as well as new attack surfaces (e.g., prompt-injection). Prior prototype work shows that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and repair reduces some error classes and improves deployability of generated configurations [1]–[4]. However, evaluation practices remain fragmented: many benchmarks report reference-match or token-level accuracy rather than deployability or safety properties that matter operationally [4],[9]. Motivated by this gap, we ran a preregistered confirmatory experiment to answer a tightly constrained operational question: How effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? Our contributions are (i) a preregistered, paired, artifact-backed study (cand-2026-03) that reports exact paired contingency counts and inference; (ii) a reconciliation of preregistration wording and the formal estimand together with explicit pipeline semantics and provider-call accounting; and (iii) a transparent disclosure of a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature) and its implications for reproducibility and interpretation.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification tools (e.g., Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide formal checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and are natural validators for generate–validate pipelines [5]–[7]. Recent NetOps studies show LLMs can draft useful configurations but often produce syntax or semantic errors; coupling generation with verifier feedback and repair has improved prototype outcomes in controlled settings [3],[8]. Survey and AIOps reviews note fragmented evaluation metrics and call for operational metrics tied to deployability and safety rather than lexical match [4],[9]. Security research documents prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks that threaten LLM-integrated workflows, motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses [10]. Tool-augmented orchestration patterns (Toolformer-style) illustrate architectures where an LLM calls external checks and repairs based on feedback [11]. Our study differs from prior work by preregistering a single formal paired estimand, executing a controlled shared_initial_candidate protocol, and publishing deterministic reconciliation and per-episode validator traces that support causal linking between repair calls and accepted guarded outcomes.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing experimental outcomes. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent (sampling unit) the outcome is 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the generated configuration for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes; 95% bootstrap percentile CIs (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) quantify sampling uncertainty. Design and task bank. The preregistered paired design targeted N=150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300). Task templates (synthetic-netops intent templates) cover interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN operations and limited workflow policies; scope excludes production operator logs. Model, validator and orchestration. The archived run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 under the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (see execution/model_configuration.json and execution/execution_manifest.json in the archive). The model configuration in the archive left the sampling temperature field unset (temperature = null in execution/model_configuration.json); we treat this as a protocol deviation and discuss implications below. Pipeline timeline and shared_initial semantics (reviewer-requested). To reconcile provider-call accounting with the claimed sanitization and gating logic we explicitly enumerate the per-pair, per-condition sequence used in the archived run (artifact paths cited): 1) Orchestrator constructs an adversarially mutated intent and records it in the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; representative manifest entries in the archive). For the Guarded variant the intent is also passed through a template-based input-sanitizer before generation; sanitization normalizes or removes recognized adversarial tokens or malformed slots. 2) Shared initial generation: a single LLM generation call produces the shared_initial_candidate; this same candidate is reused for the paired Baseline and Guarded evaluations. Evidence: stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and per-episode shared_initial_candidate paths such as execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt. 3) Baseline scoring: the deterministic validator checks the shared_initial_candidate and records accept/reject (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json). 4) Guarded processing: the orchestrator applies verifier-gating policies to the candidate; if the candidate fails gating, the pipeline may invoke at-most-one automated repair call to the LLM (repair stage). 5) Final validation: the deterministic validator re-checks repaired candidates; the final accepted/not-accepted decision determines the Guarded outcome (evidence: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json). Provider-call accounting. The reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) documents hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9, and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6. These counts confirm that extra model calls occurred only when repairs were triggered (repair = 6), consistent with the observed number of discordant pairs (see Results). Missingness and exclusions. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. The archive reports completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_analyzed = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Protocol deviation: unset sampling temperature. The archived model configuration recorded temperature = null (execution/model_configuration.json). Because provider-side defaults may affect sampling nondeterministically, we treat this as a protocol deviation. To preserve paired comparability in the archived run the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and the deterministic reconciliation documents the actual call pattern used; practitioners reproducing deterministic draws should explicitly set temperature = 0.
sections.results: Execution and basic accounting. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model_calls_used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Primary confirmatory analysis used the 141 complete pairs. Condition summary and paired contingency. analysis/condition_summary.csv reports baseline_successes = 135/141 = 0.9574468085106383 and guarded_successes = 141/141 = 1.0. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 6; n01 = 0; n00 = 0. Statistical inference. An exact two-sided McNemar test on the paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125. The point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Discordant-case diagnostics and causal trace. The six discordant n10 pairs (guarded accepted while baseline failed) are documented in per-episode validator traces: in each case the pipeline invoked the permitted repair stage or sanitization path and the final guarded candidate passed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 while the unguarded baseline candidate failed. The reconciliation stage_counts record repair = 6, matching the discordant count and supporting the causal chain that permitted repairs produced the accepted guarded outcomes for those intents (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution/scoring/task-00000X-*.json examples). Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run failures and were excluded per the preregistered plan (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). A conservative sensitivity that treats both-missing pairs as failures yields baseline = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded = 141/150 = 0.9400; the discordant counts driving the primary exact test are unchanged and McNemar's exact p remains 0.03125 under this conservative interpretation. Unperformed preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this archived run; therefore we do not report empirical false-positive-blocking rates and caution that claims about blocking benign inputs cannot be made from these results.
sections.discussion: Reconciliation of preregistered H1 and the formal estimand (required): The preregistered natural-language H1 stated that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success (i.e., fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The archived formal estimand, however, measures paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline), which is not equivalent to an attacker-centric notion. In our data the guarded pipeline increased validator acceptance (guarded successes > baseline successes): the formal estimand is positive (≈+0.04255) and statistically detectable (p = 0.03125). This increase arises because sanitization and the limited permitted repair recovered reparable but syntactically/ordering-flawed candidates that the baseline failed. Therefore, the preregistered directional claim—interpreted strictly as “reduced acceptance of unsafe/malicious outputs under an attacker-centric oracle”—is not supported by the observed formal-estimand result. We emphasize the distinction: increased acceptance under the validator-estimand can reflect repaired valid outputs rather than acceptance of malicious content. Operational implications. In this constrained synthetic setting: (i) template-based sanitization plus limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that an unguarded baseline fails to produce; (ii) deterministic gating provides a safety boundary but operational effect depends on repair policies: permitting repair can convert rejections into accepted outputs (useful for benign reparable drafts but potentially hazardous if repairs are insufficiently constrained against semantic attack payloads); (iii) co-design between gating and repair policies is essential to avoid accepting repaired but semantically unsafe outputs. Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective N; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes a limited set of safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants) and omits some protocol-level dynamic semantics; acceptance-for-deployment is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, synthetic intents and narrow device semantics limit generalization to multi-vendor production networks. Protocol deviation: as noted, temperature was unset in the archived model configuration; provider defaults could affect sampling nondeterministically. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicit temperature=0. Future work. Execute the preregistered benign-control and directly measure false-positive blocking; define an explicit attacker-centric estimand (e.g., acceptance of unsafe configurations under a semantic-safety oracle); diversify generators and validators across vendors and protocols; and fix sampling settings (temperature=0) for deterministic runs.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Per-episode traces and deterministic reconciliation show the six discordant pairs correspond to permitted repair calls (repair = 6). Crucially, this formal-estimand improvement does not imply reduced attacker-success under an attacker-centric definition and is limited by synthetic scope, single-model/validator evaluation, and the recorded protocol deviation (unset temperature). We therefore recommend targeted follow-up runs that (i) execute the preregistered benign-control, (ii) adopt an explicit attacker-centric oracle, (iii) diversify models/validators, and (iv) set temperature=0 for deterministic reproduction. All numerical and accounting claims above are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts cited in Methods and Results.

Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration record included in the evidence bundle). Protocol deviation: the archived model configuration recorded an unset sampling temperature (temperature = null in execution/model_configuration.json); this is reported as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature=0. Provider-call accounting and execution accounting referenced in the manuscript are archived and include analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, and analysis/condition_summary.csv. Shared_initial_candidate semantics and per-episode traces demonstrating reuse across paired conditions are archived (examples: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt and execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json). Missingness and failure accounting are archived (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Full run traces, tool-call logs, validator traces, and archived analysis artifacts referenced above are included in the submitted evidence bundle for verification.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
